options.text: Debit side of Capital A/c

card.front: At what rate is interest on a partner’s loan payable if the deed is silent?
card.back: If any partner has advanced loan to the firm for the purpose of business, he/she shall be entitled to get an interest on the loan amount at the rate of 6 per cent per annum.

question.body: Partners have no specific agreement on a matter affecting the distribution of profits. Which provisions apply in this situation?

options.text: The provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932
The terms of a specific agreement between the partners
The rules for calculating interest on drawings
The adjustments made when a partner is admitted or dies

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: What is the fixed capital method?
card.back: Under the fixed capital method, the capitals of the partners shall remain fixed unless additional capital is introduced or a part of the capital is withdrawn as per the agreement among the partners.
card.quote: Under the fixed capital method, the capitals of the partners shall remain fixed unless additional capital is introduced or a part of the capital is withdrawn as per the agreement among the partners.

question.body: Q1. In the absence of a partnership deed, interest on a partner's loan to the firm is paid at:

options.text: 6% p.a. simple interest
12% p.a. simple interest
6% per month

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: The clauses of partnership deed can be altered with the ____ of all the partners.
card.back: The clauses of partnership deed can be altered with the consent of all the partners.
card.quote: The clauses of partnership deed can be altered with the consent of all the partners.

card.subject: accountancy
card.back: But wherever it is in writing, the document, which contains terms of the agreement is called ‘Partnership Deed’.
card.quote: But wherever it is in writing, the document, which contains terms of the agreement is called ‘Partnership Deed’.

question.body: A firm maintains partners’ accounts under the fixed capital method. During the year, partner R is allocated a share of profit and makes ordinary drawings. No additional capital is introduced, and no part of R’s capital is withdrawn under the partnership agreement. What happens to R’s Capital Account during the year?

options.text: It is increased by the share of profit allocated to R.
It remains unchanged during the year.
It is reduced by the ordinary drawings made by R.
It is adjusted for both the share of profit and the ordinary drawings.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: The Partnership Act does not require that the agreement must be in ____.
card.back: The Partnership Act does not require that the agreement must be in writing.
card.quote: The Partnership Act does not require that the agreement must be in writing.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Can a partner claim interest on capital as a matter of right?
card.back: No partner is entitled to claim any interest on the amount of capital contributed by him in the firm as a matter of right.
card.quote: No partner is entitled to claim any interest on the amount of capital contributed by him in the firm as a matter of right.

question.body:
Four stages in a partnership are described below. The partners first reach an agreement orally on business terms. They then record those agreed terms in a written document. At a later stage, they decide to change one clause in that document; all partners give consent before the clause is changed. Arrange the listed events in the order they occur.
(A) All partners consent to the proposed clause change.
(B) The written document containing the agreed terms is identified as the Partnership Deed.
(C) The partners reach the agreement on the business terms.
(D) The clause is changed.
Choose the correct sequence.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: According to the Partnership Act, what is the position when the deed is silent?
card.back:
the partners share profits equally
no partner is entitled to remuneration
no interest on capital is allowed
no interest on drawings is charged
he is entitled to interest on such amount @ 6% per annum
card.quote: According to the Partnership Act, the partners share profits equally, no partner is entitled to remuneration, no interest on capital is allowed and no interest on drawings is charged. However, if any partner has given some loan to the firm, he is entitled to interest on such amount @ 6% per annum.

question.body: Leena and Farah agree orally to enter into a partnership. They have not prepared a written document. Which statement correctly describes whether their agreement must be in writing?

options.text: Their partnership cannot come into existence until the oral terms are put in writing.
Their oral agreement is itself a Partnership Deed.
Their oral agreement can establish the partnership; a written document is not compulsory.
Their partnership can come into existence without an agreement if they prepare a written deed later.
